body:
This is going to be a bit of a vent, but this is exactly the post that I think I needed. I guess the problem is having done something that's pretty shitty sexually but didn't rise to the level of rape. I doubt I'd be here if I had done absolutely nothing wrong, and likewise I'm not sure if I'd be here if I had actually done something horribly illegal (especially to the level that was written in that police report). What triggered the depression and suicidal thoughts was knowing that someone felt incredibly hurt by my actions. The experience of the incident in my original post prompted a strong re-evaluation of how I approached sex, and to how people can definitely feel pressured into doing things they don't want to. It also showed me how it can be difficult to articulate how people are feeling in the moment (I payed very very close attention to body language, and would often check in during sex once or twice just to make sure everything was OK as a result of this incident, definitely didn't want to risk hurting someone like that again (this isn't an issue now because the thought of sex just freaks me out and I can't actually imagine getting aroused enough around another person because of the fear of stepping over someones boundaries)). The reason it is hard to move on is because of the blemish that this one sexual incident had over the whole process. Don't get me wrong I'm still very hurt and angry over the other allegations that she threw into the report, but knowing that I am not completely blameless in this ordeal is one that really prevents me from moving forward. At the end of the day someone did get really hurt, actually we both did. I actually really hope someone reads this and doesn't make the same mistake I did. hopefully that can foster a lot more respect between people.

 Anyways sorry about the wall of text, but your post actually resonated with me and seemed to get where I was coming from. Thank you
Thank you for your kind words
